questions.question: What happens if the same key is used twice for the same random operation?
questions.explanation: Keys are explicit immutable inputs. Identical inputs reproduce the draw; split keys to describe independent randomness.
optionFeedback: A JAX key is an explicit value, not an advancing generator. Split it and pass a distinct key for each intended random draw.
Keys are explicit immutable inputs. Identical inputs reproduce the draw; split keys to describe independent randomness.
Key reuse need not raise an exception. Compare the actual samples; reproducibility requires managing keys even when execution succeeds.
